source_text: Liber Tertius. Prius perspici nec agnosci potest quanta sit in Verbo magnificentia, nisi prius oculos quis columbae, id est intelligentiam spiritalem, accipiat. Commune sibi cubile quod dicit esse cum sponso, corpus hoc mihi videtur indicari animae, in quo adhuc posita digna habita sit adscisci ad consortium Verbi Dei.
pass_a_gloss: Book Third. First to-be-seen nor to-be-known is-able how-great may-be in Word magnificence, unless first eyes someone of-dove, that is understanding spiritual, may-receive...
pass_b_english: The Third Book. The greatness in the Word cannot first be seen or known unless one first receives dove-eyes — that is, spiritual understanding. The couch she says she shares with the Bridegroom seems to me to indicate this body of the soul, in which, while still placed there, she has been counted worthy to be taken into the Word’s companionship.
